concept.name: Wyckoff Phase E
concept.definition: The final phase of a Wyckoff trading range, in which price departs the range and the new trend (markup or markdown) unfolds in the open, with demand or supply in full control. Setbacks are typically short-lived, and new higher- or lower-level ranges (reaccumulation or redistribution 'stepping stones') may form along the way.
concept.intuition: The range is over and the real move begins — the trend is now obvious to everyone.
concept.mechanics: Price breaks out of the trading range and trends; pullbacks after markup begins are brief and shallow, and broken support in markdown is often retested by failing rallies. Traders trail stops and may add positions at stepping-stone consolidations, whose point-and-figure counts can confirm the original range's price target.
concept.failure_modes: Breakouts into Phase E can fail, returning price to the range; as the trend matures toward the P&F objective, the risk of a new accumulation or distribution range (i.e., a reversal) increases.
concept.misconceptions: Phase E does not mean risk-free trending; Wyckoff treats P&F targets as places to 'stop, look and listen', not guaranteed endpoints, and stepping-stone ranges can turn into reversal structures.
concept.example: A stock leaves its 90-102 base and trends to 130 with only two brief pauses; the holder trails stops and watches a small mid-trend range whose count confirms the original 130 target.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
citations.section: Accumulation: Wyckoff Phases (Phase E); Distribution: Wyckoff Phases (Phase E)
